title: spec review: R8 v2: orchestrator/jev_sched.py — Jev as a shadow scheduling signal for soft-interference pairs only: batched, locked cache, [scheduler.jev] table, fail-open, never overriding deterministic constraints (AP P15)
spec:
Why: waves are deterministic (interference.select_wave) and soft pairs are deferred or admitted by rule; AP P15 / brief P10 allow Jev to answer only ambiguous questions (semantic interference, stale-assumption risk) in shadow first, without O(n^2) calls. v2 after spec review T-0616.
What: new module orchestrator/jev_sched.py using jev.ask (orchestrator/jev.py:184; returns {answers:{key:{noul, confidence}}, usage} or None) and decision_log.record(kind='jev_sched'). Tests are unittest.TestCase methods in the named file (this repo runs unittest; no pytest fixtures).
- PAIR_QUESTIONS = {'semantic_interference': {'type': 'noul', 'instructions': 'Probability that these two tasks change the same behaviour or interface and would conflict if run concurrently'}, 'stale_assumption_risk': {'type': 'noul', 'instructions': 'Probability that finishing one task first invalidates assumptions the other relies on'}} (the dict shape jev.ask requires, as in jev_route.QUESTIONS). ambiguous_pairs(pairwise_rows) -> only rows with level soft whose reasons contain no 'dependency:' kind; hard and none are never asked.
- cfg: nested table [scheduler.jev] read as (pool_config().get('scheduler') or {}).get('jev') or {} with keys mode off|shadow|active (default shadow; unknown -> shadow), max_pairs 8, cache_ttl_s 3600, cache_max_entries 200 (mirrors [jev.routing] in jev_route._routing_cfg). No pool.toml edit; defaults in code.
- Privacy: the per-pair state is {a, b, titles, scope (the tasks' scope path lists, allowed: paths are metadata), spec excerpts spec[:400] passed through jev.redact, interference reasons}; never file contents, diffs or worktree reads (the module performs no file or git reads at all).
- One jev.ask per annotate() call with at most max_pairs pairs, questions keyed '<a>|<b>:<question>'; state is the list of pair dicts.
- Cache: STATE/runs/jev/sched_cache.json keyed sha1(sorted pair ids + scope tuples + goal_head); read/write with the same fcntl-locked sidecar (.lock) plus tempfile.mkstemp + os.replace discipline as jev_route._cache_read/_cache_write; TTL and cache_max_entries pruning; a different goal_head or scope misses.
- annotate(wave_result, pairwise_rows, tasks, *, goal_head, cfg=None, root=STATE, ask=jev.ask) -> {'mode', 'asked', 'cache': hit|miss|None, 'signals': {'a|b': {semantic_interference, stale_assumption_risk, confidence}}, 'would_defer': [ids Jev rates semantic_interference >= 0.7 for a pair whose members are both in the wave; the later one in wave order is listed], 'applied': [], 'wave', 'deferred', 'error': None|reason}. off -> input unchanged, asked 0, no ask call. shadow -> computes would_defer, changes nothing. active -> moves would_defer ids from wave to deferred with reason 'jev:<a>|<b>'; it only removes from the wave (never adds, never touches hard-deferred or dependency pairs, never exceeds capacity); any failure (ask None, malformed, value outside [0,1]) -> error set, wave and deferred returned unchanged (fail open).
- Every annotate call with asked > 0 or mode active records decision_log.record(kind='jev_sched', subject=<goal id of the first candidate or first task id>, candidates=pair keys, hard_constraints=['dependency', 'hard_conflicts', 'capacity'], deterministic={'wave', 'deferred'}, jev=signals, selected=applied, rejected=would_defer, reason, confidence=mean confidence, n=asked, mode).
acceptance: tests/test_jev_sched.py::test_off_mode_never_calls_jev_and_returns_wave_unchanged — mode off: ask not called, asked 0, wave and deferred identical

tests/test_jev_sched.py::test_shadow_mode_records_would_defer_without_changing_wave — a soft pair rated 0.9 lands in would_defer, applied empty, wave unchanged, and a jev_sched decision row is written

tests/test_jev_sched.py::test_active_mode_defers_soft_pair_but_never_hard_or_dependency — active: the soft-pair task moves to deferred with reason jev:<a>|<b>; a hard pair and a soft pair carrying a dependency reason are never asked and never changed

tests/test_jev_sched.py::test_fail_open_and_single_batched_call_without_n_squared — ask returning None yields error set and the deterministic wave; with 12 soft pairs ask is called once with at most max_pairs pairs and no hard or none pair appears in the questions

tests/test_jev_sched.py::test_cache_locking_invalidation_and_privacy — the same pairs and goal_head hit the cache (ask called once across two calls) and a sidecar .lock file exists; a new goal_head misses; the state passed to ask contains only titles, scope paths, redacted spec excerpts and reasons, no file contents (a marker string planted in a scope file's contents never appears), and jev.redact was applied

risks.issue: promotion.py already registers a feature exactly named 'jev_sched' with config path table='scheduler', key='jev_mode' (a flat key on the existing [scheduler] table, alongside mode/soft_conflict_policy/max_wave/stale_rebase). The spec instead has annotate() read a nested [scheduler.jev] table with a 'mode' sub-key. These are two different config locations for the same feature: promotion.current_mode('jev_sched', cfg) will read scheduler.jev_mode and always report the default ('shadow') regardless of what an operator sets under [scheduler.jev].mode, and setting [scheduler.jev].mode has zero effect on the promotion/evidence tooling's view of the feature. This silently breaks the shadow->active promotion workflow for this exact feature with no error.

collect(feature='jev_sched') sources evidence from runs/sched/waves.jsonl and runs/sched/stale.jsonl, not from decision_log rows (kind='jev_sched'). The spec's only evidence trail is decision_log.record(kind='jev_sched', ...); nothing in scope updates waves.jsonl/stale.jsonl, so promotion.evaluate('jev_sched', ...) will keep seeing n=0/insufficient_evidence forever even after annotate() runs repeatedly in shadow mode. Worth confirming this is intentional (a separate future wiring task) rather than an oversight.

Spec doesn't specify how the per-pair 'confidence' in signals (one value) is derived from the two sub-question confidences (semantic_interference, stale_assumption_risk) each pair asks. Undefined aggregation (e.g. average vs min vs first) is exactly the kind of ambiguity that produces divergent executor/reviewer interpretations and an acceptance test that can't be pinned down.

suggested_spec_changes: Change the cfg read to match the pre-existing promotion.py contract: read mode from (pool_config().get('scheduler') or {}).get('jev_mode', 'shadow') instead of introducing a new nested [scheduler.jev].mode table; keep max_pairs/cache_ttl_s/cache_max_entries as sibling flat keys on [scheduler] (e.g. jev_max_pairs, jev_cache_ttl_s, jev_cache_max_entries) for consistency with mode/soft_conflict_policy/max_wave/stale_rebase already on that table.

Either wire a decision_log-based (or waves.jsonl-based) evidence source into promotion.collect('jev_sched') in this same task, or explicitly note in the spec that promotion evidence collection for jev_sched is out of scope and left returning n=0 until a follow-up task.

Specify the per-pair confidence aggregation rule explicitly (e.g. 'None if either sub-question confidence is None, else the mean of the two', mirroring jev_route.classify's confidence averaging) so the acceptance test's expected confidence values are unambiguous.
